entries.title: Ganesa Macula
entries.extract: Ganesa Macula is a dark feature on Saturn's moon Titan. It is named after the Hindu god Ganesha.

entries.title: Xanadu (Titan)
entries.extract: Xanadu is a highly reflective area on the leading hemisphere of Saturn's moon Titan. Its name comes from an alternate transcription of Shangdu, the summer capital of the Yuan dynasty established by Kublai Khan and made famous by Samuel Taylor Coleridge.

entries.title: Adiri (Titan)
entries.extract: Adiri is a large, bright albedo feature on Saturn's moon Titan. It is named after the paradise in Melanesian mythology. It is located to the west of the large, dark region of Shangri-la.

entries.title: Dilmun (Titan)
entries.extract: Dilmun is a region of high albedo on Titan, Saturn's natural satellite. It was discovered in the images transmitted by the Cassini spacecraft. It received the name of Dilmun, the garden paradise in Sumerian mythology.

entries.title: Mezzoramia (Titan)
entries.extract: Mezzoramia is a dark albedo feature (region) located at 70°S 0°W on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. It is named after Mezzoramia, a mythical African oasis of happiness from Italian legend.

entries.title: Shangri-La (Titan)
entries.extract: Shangri-La is a large, dark region of Saturn's moon Titan at 10°S 165°W. It is named after Shangri-La, the mythical paradise in Tibet.

entries.title: Tsegihi
entries.extract: Tsegihi is a bright region in Titan's southern mid-latitudes. It is centered at 40°S 10°W.

entries.title: Santorini Facula
entries.extract: The Santorini Facula is a facula, or bright spot, surrounding a 40-km-wide impact crater on the surface of Titan. It was named after the Greek island Santorini in 2006.

entries.title: Shikoku Facula
entries.extract: Shikoku Facula is a region of bright material on Saturn's moon Titan.

entries.title: Ontario Lacus
entries.extract: Ontario Lacus is a lake composed of methane, ethane, propane, and butane near the south pole of Saturn's moon Titan. Its character as a hydrocarbon lake was confirmed by observations from the Cassini spacecraft, published in the 31 July 2008 edition of Nature.

entries.title: Hotei Arcus
entries.extract: Hotei Arcus is a prominent arcus on Titan, a moon of Saturn.The arcus was named after Budai, the god of happiness in Japanese Buddhism. He is the god of contentment, good fortune, cheerfulness, and he is always smiling. The name "Hotei" was officially approved by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2006.

entries.title: Guabonito (crater)
entries.extract: Guabonito is a ring of bright features on Saturn's moon Titan. Currently, the feature is thought to be a partially buried impact crater, with the bright features representing the crater's rim.

entries.title: Tui Regio
entries.extract: Tui Regio is a region on Titan, the Saturnian moon, in the southwest corner of Xanadu, named after Tui, a Chinese goddess of happiness, joy and water. Tui appears to lack the erosion channels that mark other highland regions on Titan, suggesting it may be geologically young.

entries.title: Perkunas Virgae
entries.extract: Perkunas Virgae is a streak of colour on Titan, the natural satellite of Saturn, centred at 27° latitude south and 162 longitude west. It measures 980 km at its widest point. It was discovered in images transmitted by the Cassini mission and named after Perkūnas, the main rain god of Lithuanian mythology.

entries.title: Menrva (crater)
entries.extract: Menrva is the largest crater on Titan, with a diameter of 392 kilometers. The crater is a heavily eroded double ringed impact basin, similar to the impact related features of Mars and Mercury. This is evident by Menrva's distinct lack of a central peak, indicating modification of the crater's surface since formation.

entries.title: Sinlap
entries.extract: Sinlap is a shallow impact crater on Titan, a natural satellite of Saturn. Located in the Fensal region, Sinlap is one of the most pristine craters on Titan, surrounded by a bright ejecta blanket.

entries.title: Elivagar Flumina
entries.extract: Elivagar Flumina is a network of river channels, known as flumina, located in the region around the Menrva Crater of Titan. These channels range in length from 23 km to 210 km and are at least 120 km wide, showing signs of erosion. At their mouth, an alluvial fan is present.

entries.title: Abaya Lacus
entries.extract: Abaya Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

entries.title: Bolsena Lacus
entries.extract: Bolsena Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

entries.title: Feia Lacus
entries.extract: Feia Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon seas and lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan. It was named in 2007 on the basis of data taken by the space probe Cassini.

entries.title: Koitere Lacus
entries.extract: Koitere Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan. The lake is composed of liquid methane and ethane, and was detected by the space probe Cassini.

entries.title: Mackay Lacus
entries.extract: Mackay Lacus is the seventh largest of a number of hydrocarbon seas and lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan. The lake is composed of liquid methane and ethane, and was detected by the Cassini space probe.

entries.title: Neagh Lacus
entries.extract: Neagh Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan. The lake is composed of liquid methane and ethane, and was detected by the Cassini space probe.

entries.title: Sotonera Lacus
entries.extract: Sotonera Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

entries.title: Selk (crater)
entries.extract: Selk is a crater on Titan, a moon of Saturn, located at 7°N 199°W. It is a geologically young impact crater that measures approximately 90 kilometres (56 mi) in diameter. It was discovered in 2004 by the Cassini–Huygens mission during its first Titan flyby.

entries.title: Kraken Mare
entries.extract: Kraken Mare is the largest known hydrocarbon sea on the surface of Saturn's moon Titan. It was discovered by the space probe Cassini in 2006, and was named in 2008 after the Kraken, a legendary sea monster.

entries.title: Ligeia Mare
entries.extract: Ligeia Mare is a lake in the north polar region of Titan, the planet Saturn's largest moon. It is the second largest body of liquid on the surface of Titan, after Kraken Mare. Larger than Lake Superior on Earth, it is mostly composed of liquid methane.

entries.title: Mayda Insula
entries.extract: Mayda Insula is an island in the Kraken Mare, a body of liquid composed primarily of methane, on Saturn's largest moon Titan. Mayda Insula is the first island (insula) to be named on a planet or moon other than Earth.

entries.title: Kivu Lacus
entries.extract: Kivu Lacus is a small Titanean hydrocarbon lake. It was discovered by the Cassini probe. The lake is near Titan's north pole and is named after Lake Kivu in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda. In 2012, Cassini spotted an Infrared glint off the lake. The aspects of it suggested waves.

entries.title: Punga Mare
entries.extract: Punga Mare is a lake in the north polar region of Titan, the planet Saturn's largest moon. After Kraken Mare and Ligeia Mare, it is the third largest known body of liquid on Titan. It is composed of liquid hydrocarbons.7° W, it measures roughly 380 km (236 mi) across, greater than the length of Lake Victoria on Earth.

entries.title: Jingpo Lacus
entries.extract: Jingpo Lacus is a lake in the north polar region of Titan, the planet Saturn's largest moon. It and similarly sized Ontario Lacus are the largest known bodies of liquid on Titan after the three maria. It is composed of liquid hydrocarbons.

entries.title: Arrakis Planitia
entries.extract: Arrakis Planitia is a planitia (plain) on Titan, the largest natural satellite of the planet Saturn. It is located in Titan's southern hemisphere, between 74 and 80° south and 113–134° east, within the Mezzoramia region.

entries.title: Albano Lacus
entries.extract: Albano Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

entries.title: Eyre Lacuna
entries.extract: Eyre Lacuna is a feature on Saturn's largest moon, Titan, believed to be a currently dry bed of an intermittent hydrocarbon lake.

entries.title: Ngami Lacuna
entries.extract: Ngami Lacuna is a feature on Saturn's largest moon, Titan, believed to be the currently dry bed of an intermittent hydrocarbon lake.

entries.title: Doom Mons
entries.extract: Doom Mons is the name of a mountain range and its eponymous peak on Titan, the largest moon of Saturn. A putative cryovolcano, it is the largest mountain range on Titan by volume. It was discovered by the Cassini–Huygens probe in 2005 and officially named in 2012.

entries.title: Erebor Mons
entries.extract: Erebor Mons is a mountain on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn.23°W, in the western part of Quivira region. It is 40 km across, more than 1 km high, and has lobate flow features to its north and east. It is probably a cryovolcano.

entries.title: Irensaga Montes
entries.extract: The Irensaga Montes is a range of mountains on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. The range is located near Titan's equator, between 5–6° south and 210–214° east. It is located within the Adiri region, just west of the landing site of the Huygens probe.

entries.title: Mindolluin Montes
entries.extract: The Mindolluin Montes are a range of mountains on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. The range is located near Titan's equator, between 1–4° south and 205–213° east. It is located within the Adiri region, just west of the landing site of the Huygens probe.

entries.title: Misty Montes
entries.extract: The Misty Montes are a range of mountains on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. The range is located in the northern hemisphere of Titan, between 56–7° north and 61–3° west.

entries.title: Mithrim Montes
entries.extract: The Mithrim Montes are a range of mountains on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. The range is located near Titan's equator, between 1–3° south and 126–8° west and consists of three parallel ridges that are oriented east–west, spaced about 25 km apart. They are located within the region Xanadu.

entries.title: Taniquetil Montes
entries.extract: The Taniquetil Montes are a mountain range on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. The range is located near Titan's equator, between 2° and 4° south, and 211° and 214° west. It is located within the Adiri region, just west of the landing site of the Huygens probe.

entries.title: Arwen Colles
entries.extract: Arwen Colles is an area of small hills on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. The hills are located near Titan's equator at 7.5°S 260°W within the Belet region.

entries.title: Bilbo Colles
entries.extract: Bilbo Colles is an area of small hills on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. The hills are located near Titan's equator at 4.23°S 38.56°W on western edge of bright region Quivira.

entries.title: Faramir Colles
entries.extract: Faramir Colles is an area of small hills on Titan, the largest moon of the planet Saturn. The hills are located near Titan's equator at 4° north and 153° east within the Shangri-La region.

entries.title: Sotra Patera
entries.extract: Sotra Patera is a prominent depression on Titan, the largest moon of Saturn. It was formerly known as Sotra Facula; the current name was approved on 19 December 2012.90 mi) high Doom Mons. Sotra Patera is the deepest known pit on Titan.

entries.title: Vid Flumina
entries.extract: Vid Flumina is a river system of liquid methane and ethane on Saturn's moon Titan. It is more than 400 km (249 mi) long and flows into Titan's second largest hydrocarbon sea, Ligeia Mare.

entries.title: Sionascaig Lacus
entries.extract: Sionascaig Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon seas and lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan. The lake is located at latitude 41.52°S and longitude 278.12°W on Titan's globe, and is composed of liquid methane and ethane. The feature is named for the Earth lake, Loch Sionascaig, in Scotland.

entries.title: Ladoga Lacus
entries.extract: Ladoga Lacus is a geographical feature on Saturn's largest moon, Titan, named after Lake Ladoga, Russia. It is one of a number of "methane lakes" found in Titan's north polar region.

entries.title: Hammar Lacus
entries.extract: Hammar Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon seas and lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

entries.title: Müggel Lacus
entries.extract: Müggel Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon seas and lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

entries.title: Kutch Lacuna
entries.extract: Kutch Lacuna is a large intermittent lake on Titan.

entries.title: Nakuru Lacuna
entries.extract: Nakuru Lacuna is the largest intermittent lake on Titan.

entries.title: Woytchugga Lacuna
entries.extract: Woytchugga Lacuna is one of the largest lakes of Titan.

entries.title: Saraswati Flumen
entries.extract: Saraswati Flumen is a river system of liquid methane and ethane on Saturn's moon Titan. It flows for 360 km before discharging into Ontario Lacus near Titan's south pole in a river delta on the lake's western shore.

entries.title: Lakes and rivers of Titan
entries.extract: Lakes of liquid ethane and methane exist on the surface of Titan, Saturn's largest moon. This was confirmed by the Cassini–Huygens space probe, and had been suspected long before. The large bodies of liquid are known as maria (seas) and the small ones as lacūs (lakes).

entries.title: Akmena Lacus
entries.extract: Abaya Lacus is one of a number of hydrocarbon lakes found on Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

entries.title: Ahmakiq Undae
entries.extract: Ahmakiq Undae is a massive undae, or dune field, on Saturn's largest moon, Titan. It is located at Titan's equator and is the future initial landing site of the Dragonfly probe.
